A fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Capcom. Mega Man and Battle Network are Capcom's; the game runs from the ROMs you own and none of it is distributed here. The start's chime is "UI Success Chime" by SoundShelfStudio, from Pixabay.

These notes with their pictures are on the project's website and GitHub.

1729049.html:
The eighth beta: with BN5 Team Colonel's ROM beside BN6's, its net is no longer a second game run beside this one. BN5's viruses, guardians, chips, Souls and DarkChips fight in BN6's own battle engine, by their own code from your ROM, with BN6's HUD, Custom screen, Crosses and Beast Out around them. Plus saves that move between systems, a soft reset that stays in the game, a smoother New 3DS, and the site in Japanese.

⚔️ One Battle Network

BN5's net, fought in BN6's engine

In 0.11, a battle in one of BN5's areas handed the screen to a second emulator running BN5 itself, with its own rules, its own HUD and no Crosses. Now every battle is BN6's. BN5's 25 virus families that BN6 lacks are moved from your BN5 ROM into BN6's battle engine by their own code, and each was checked frame by frame against BN5's own battles before it shipped. They fight beside BN6's HUD and Custom screen, and everything MegaMan carries works against them.

Where BN5's ROM sits beside BN6's, each of its areas takes the place of a BN6 area in about half the runs: ACDC for Central, Oran for Green, SciLab for Sky, End Area for Seaside, its Undernet for the Undernet, and Nebula for the Graveyard. (#82)

BN5's guardians

ToadMan, KnightMan, ShadowMan, NumberMan, TomahawkMan and Colonel guard acts in BN5's areas, fought in BN6's engine at BN6's guardians' strength, no longer three quarters of it. So does the Dark Soul.

Souls, in every battle

A BN5 guardian deleted gives his Soul for the run. UNITE on the Custom screen, giving up a chip of the Soul's kind, makes MegaMan that Soul for three turns, in any battle, BN6's areas too: its look, its charged shot and its passive, as BN5 has them. One form at a time: UNITE and Beast Out share the emblem's slot. Chaos Unison goes as BN5's does: a DarkChip comes while MegaMan worries, and UNITE stays dark while he does, so keep it, calm him with a chip that lands, and give it up on the next Custom screen. A DarkChip given up for Chaos Unison costs no max HP.

DarkChips from the flames

BN5's flames of darkness stand on its areas' layers, and their DarkChips come by BN5's rule: dealt while MegaMan is worried, at a quarter of his HP or hit again and again. Every battle a DarkChip runs in costs 20 max HP for the rest of the dive, and MegaMan says so before you take one. DarkInvs hands MegaMan to the game for ten seconds, grey and untouchable, as BN5's does. DarkPlus adds 50 to the next chip.

Lava and sea

BN5's lava and sea panels work in BN6's battles as they do in BN5: lava burns what stands on it unless it is Fire, and the sea holds back whatever is not Aqua.

Where the nets meet

From act 2, a battle in four may bring a visitor from the other net: BN5's viruses in BN6's areas, BN6's in BN5's. The deep acts draw from both nets, and BN5's chips are chips of the run, one chip per name, in shops, traders, rewards and Mystery Data.

On the New 3DS too

The New 3DS reads BN5's ROM where its heap has room for it. Put Team Colonel beside BN6's ROM and BN5's net joins your runs there as everywhere else. A 3DS without BN5 gets 16 MB of its heap back.

💾 Saves move between systems

SAVES on the title (L, or Q on a keyboard) writes your profile and the run's checkpoint to one file, cyberworld-endless.cwsave, and reads one in on any other system: a PC, a phone, a handheld, a New 3DS or the browser. It shows both saves side by side, keeps yours unless you choose the file's, and UNDO IMPORT brings them back. Controls, screen and volumes stay on each device. A newer build's file, a damaged one, or a BN5 run without BN5 is refused before anything changes. On phones the automatic copy in your ROM folder never writes over another device's file: the game asks once which saves to keep. (#114)

🔁 A soft reset that stays in the game

A+B+Select+Start reset BN6 to its own title while the run went on underneath, and going back in could put MegaMan elsewhere on the map. Now it returns to this game's title, in a battle too, and CONTINUE takes the run up at its last checkpoint. Thanks to Mattwj for the report. (#113)

🎮 A smoother New 3DS

  • No freeze at a save. A checkpoint wrote its ten files on the frame that saved, and on the 3DS's SD card that held the game still for up to a second at every layer. A thread of its own writes them now. In a six-minute run on a New 3DS, the stalls of 0.6 to 1.5 seconds went from 20 to none.
  • The act's card at full speed. Its text went through the software renderer one letter at a time, and the card dropped the game to about 40 frames a second as it showed. A line of text is drawn once and blended whole now: the seconds with the card on screen ran at 56.6 frames a second, up from 40.8.

🌐 The site in Japanese

The home page, the downloads, the FAQ and the browser player have Japanese pages, written for Japan's players, who know the game as ロックマンエグゼ6, with BN6's names as Capcom's Japanese releases write them.

Under the hood

BN5's battles in BN6's engine are held to BN5's own by a differential: each of 366 specs fights the same battle in BN5's engine and in BN6's and compares them frame by frame. 363 pass, and the three others stop where they are recorded to. Each of 167 deliberate breaks in the moved code fails its spec. The repository holds numbers only (addresses, ids, checksums); everything BN5's comes from your ROM as the game starts.

These notes with their pictures are on the project's website and GitHub.

1729050.html:
The ninth beta: your MegaMan meets other players' now. A gate in Lan's HP leads to a Net Square on a server, eight operators a channel: say a phrase, trade a spare chip at Trade Central, NetBattle each other with the MegaMen your runs built, watch from the stands, and dive the week's DeepNet, the same net for everyone. Every system goes online, the browser and the New 3DS too. Plus a leaner first act that opens up as you go deeper, and an Order Service that sorts.

🌐 The Net Square

Through the gate in Lan's HP

The way there is the great white gate at the front of Lan's HP, where every run begins and comes home between acts. The first time, the Mr.Prog who keeps it asks for the name other players will see, says what the server learns (your PET's address, that name, and MegaMan as he is) and asks before you go, the cursor on No. After that MegaMan asks each time, and Yes saves the run right there. R, or the pad you arrived by, takes you home, MegaMan back on the gate as he left it; if the game was closed in the Square, the next CONTINUE puts him there.

Your run waits at the gate. The Square has no battles of the net, no heal, no shop and no saves, and nothing there makes a run stronger: the one thing that comes home is a chip you traded. (#120)

A dropped connection waits for you

When the Square stops answering (a hiccup in your Wi-Fi, a server restarting), the game no longer sends you home. MegaMan holds still where he stands, Reconnecting... shows over the Square, and the game tries again for up to 30 seconds while the server keeps your spot, so the others see your MegaMan stay put; you play on as soon as the link is back, and B goes home at once. A NetBattle under way ends with no result and a trade not yet done is off, as on any leave; a trade you both agreed to still comes home. The gate also tells you when a newer version is out, when the Square's server is the older one, and when it is down for maintenance, with the host's own line. (#153)

The Square: phrases, a greeter, a parade and its own music

A plaza in one of BN6's daylight nets (Central, Sky or Green Area, by the server), with a landmark in its middle (a statue, a monument or a giant cybertree), a stage up a stair, the log-in plaza with its board and the pad home, Trade Central, and the Arena's ring with room to watch from. Up to eight players a channel; the gate's keeper moves you to the next or the last.

  • L has MegaMan say a phrase or do an emote over his head, for the whole channel to see. Phrases come from a fixed list: there is no free text, and no one can type at you. Say something together round the landmark or on the stage, and the Square cheers.
  • A facing another player's MegaMan shows his card (HP, act and layer, Crosses and Souls), and lets you ask him for a NetBattle, wave, mute or block him.
  • A greeter Mr.Prog calls out who logs in, each arrival in BN6's own log-in beam. Two Navis stroll about and talk about who's here and what just happened, and every three minutes they parade round the landmark: walk with them.
  • The board lists who's here, the last trade and NetBattle, the trade offers up and this week's DeepNet. A on a tree, the landmark or the sign says what it is.
  • Its own music: whatever area it stands in, the Square plays BN6's Navi Customizer theme. (#155)

The NetPass

One rule says what is open to you online, and a NetPass in Lan's PET shows it as four stamps:

StampWhat it opensWhat it needs
SquareWalking, phrases and emotes, cheering, cards, the referee's calls, the board and its posts, reading the trade offers, the week's rankingBN6 Cybeast Gregar (USA): everyone has it
ArenaNetBattles, and watching themThe full set
TradeTrading at Trade Central, and posting or answering a trade offerThe full set
DeepNetThe week's DeepNet diveThe full set

The full set is every game this version supports online: BN6 Cybeast Gregar (USA) and BN5 Team Colonel (USA). With BN5's ROM beside BN6's, all four stamps are yours, and the greeter stamps them on your next visit. With BN6's alone you hold the Square stamp: the whole Square but NetBattles, trades and the dive. If a later version supports another game online, the stamps that need it open again until you add that game, and the release notes and the site will say so ahead of time.

KeyItem in the PET, then A on NetPass, opens it; in the Square, where the PET stays shut, START does. It also shows across the top of the screen while MegaMan asks about going, and on a second screen (the New 3DS's bottom screen, an Android handheld's second display) while you are in the Square. (#131)

🤝 Trade Central

Trade Central, a desk in a wing off the plaza, trades one of your spare chips (copies beyond those in your folders) for another player's, one for one. It has two screens of its own, modelled on the Legacy Collection's:

  • The spares list, where every chip for a trade is picked: your spares with their codes and counts, beside a card of the chip under the cursor (its picture, code, element, damage and description, read from your ROM, BN5's chips too). START sorts them by ID, ABCDE or Code.
  • The chip trade: both chips, You and Them, No deal and Deal!, the cursor on No deal. Once you both say Deal!, the cards swap places to BN6's jingle, and the chips change hands as you come home.

One trade a visit. The trade board, at the same desk, puts one spare up with what you want for it (anything, a chip of an element, a Sword, Wind, Break or Cursor chip, or a Mega), and everyone in your channel reads it, there and on the log-in plaza's board, until you take it down, leave or trade. To answer an offer, pick it at the desk: the spares list shows only your chips that fit its want. (#145)

⚔️ NetBattles, with rollback

Battle on another player's card, where you both hold the Arena stamp, asks him for a Practice NetBattle, BN6's own over an emulated link cable. You fight with your MegaMen as your runs built them: HP, NaviCust, buster, Crosses, the folder with BN5's chips in it, and your Souls (UNITE on the Custom screen as in a run, and the other player sees your Soul too). Where more than one of your folders holds chips, MegaMan asks which goes. Win or lose, you are back in the Square where you stood, and nothing is won or lost. MegaMan then asks whether to go again with the same player, the cursor on No.

The battle answers your presses with rollback: each game runs it at once, guessing the other player's buttons as the last ones he held, and when his real presses come in otherwise, it rewinds the frames that guessed wrong and plays them again. On a good connection that is 2 frames of input delay. Each system measures how far it can rewind and asks the server for the delay its connection still needs; the longer of the two players' needs is the battle's. Running both players' GBAs got three times cheaper on the way, so even the Retroid Nova rewinds up to 7 frames within a frame's time. (#128)

The stands

The referee Mr.Prog by the Arena's ring calls each NetBattle in your channel: who fights whom, their HP, the last chips they used, how many watch, the winner. With the Arena stamp he asks whether to watch, and the screen turns to the battle itself, a moment behind the players and from its first frame however late you came. R shows the other side, L cheers, B takes you back. The players hear the cheers from him after their battle. (#128)

🏆 The week's DeepNet

Every Monday (00:00 UTC) each server opens a net of its own for the week, and everyone on that server who dives it dives the same net, from the same start: the short net, the Standard folder, threat 0, no helpers and no Cross, nothing your other runs unlocked. The greeter in the log-in plaza offers it to a pass with the DeepNet stamp; the dive begins in Lan's room, as a new game does.

Your run in progress waits in a save of its own, untouched, and the title's CONTINUE stays with it. Talk to the greeter again to go on with an unfinished dive or start it over. How deep you got goes up on the board at your next visit: the week's eight deepest dives as reported, your own best and its place, and last week's three. Dive as often as you like; your best counts. A dive unlocks nothing, and nothing is won for one. (#127)

📱 Every system online

The Square, Trade Central and the DeepNet are on every system: computers, phones and tablets, PortMaster handhelds, the Steam Deck, the New 3DS and the browser.

  • NetBattles in the browser. The browser build battles in the Square as the other systems do, rollback and watching from the stands included, against another browser or a game on a computer.
  • The New 3DS has no NetBattles. Running a NetBattle's two GBAs takes it about 26 ms a frame, half again the 16.7 a frame has, so it offers no Battle and no watching, and its pass says so: "Every game in! No NetBattles on this PET." The referee still calls the channel's battles to it, and with BN5's ROM it trades and dives. Running the two GBAs on two of its cores is what is left to try (#147).

🖥️ The official server, and your own

The gate offers the official Net Square first: Saschb2b's, at cyberworld.saschb2b.com, a hobby server with no guarantees. It asks for no account and no e-mail. There is no free text, so there is nothing to report: block a name from his card, and that MegaMan is gone from your Square. It keeps its trades for 14 days and the week's board for 2 weeks, by a key your game makes for that server alone and the name you chose, its daily totals with no names for a year, and no log of who came and went. Its rules, who moderates it, what it keeps and for how long, and how to have your data removed are in its policy. (#132)

Anyone can run a Net Square of their own: the server is a small ROM-free program in Python, with ready builds for Linux, Windows and macOS beside this release (or the zipapp, for any system with Python 3.11) and a recipe for a container, and it never needs a ROM or sees a save (server/README.md). Each server has its own channels, moderators and week's DeepNet; give its address to the gate's keeper to go there. For hosts: a server prunes what it keeps by itself, at its start and every hour (trade_days, board_weeks, log_days in server.ini), --admin forget takes a player out of every record but a ban or a mute, --admin hide takes an entry off the week's board, and --backup DIR archives the server's key, moderation and board once a day, --restore putting one back. A dropped player's place is held for 40 seconds (hold and resume in the log), and maintenance = until 14:00 UTC in server.ini turns games away with that line. A 0.13.0 game speaks protocol v10: a game and a server of other versions refuse each other.

Online statistics

Where you said yes to the anonymous statistics, the same answer now covers online play, so that the Square's servers and the NetBattles' rollback are tuned on real networks: how a visit to a Net Square ended and its minutes, your NetPass and whether the server was the official one (never its address); a NetBattle's network numbers (input delay, rollback window, rollbacks and the deepest, the longest tick, the stalls) and how it ended; and that a trade was done, a battle watched or a dive posted. Never your name or another's, your identity on a server, the chips, the phrases or anything typed. Said no, nothing is sent.

For hosts: a server counts each UTC day's joins, how many different players (a number only: the day's identities are held in memory and dropped at its end), the most online at once, trades, NetBattles, battles watched, dives posted, and joins by version and by NetPass, with no names, in stats.jsonl for stats_days (365) and at GET /stats, today and the last 30 days. (#156)

💰 A leaner first act that opens up as you go deeper

The first act used to hand out about twelve chips, many in your folder's codes, and more zenny than its dealer's answer chip and HPMemory cost together, so there was little left to want or to trade. Now:

  • the first act lays half the green Mystery Data, and a green data holds a chip less often, zenny in its place;
  • the plain finds (green and blue data, a dealer's shelf, a request) hold fewer 3-star, Mega and Giga chips;
  • finds hold half the zenny;
  • no find leans to your folder's codes.

Each of these opens act by act, back to what it was by the sixth act (the short net's third), never past it. A blue data at a detour's end stays the layer's prize, and BN6's own battle rewards are untouched, so a high busting level pays as it did. Measured over 300 runs of the endless net:

Act 1BeforeNow
Chips12.29.5
Good chips (3 stars or more, Mega, Giga)3.22.2
Mystery Data14.811.6
Zenny3,5502,630
The most chips of one code, with the *s53
Chips found in the folder's codes or *63%35%

At the act's dealer you now buy the answer's two copies or the HPMemory, not both. The Chip and BugFrag Traders pick a prize's code as BN6's own Chip Trader does, three times in four one you hold none of, rather than your folder's: your codes are your run's own, and worth a trade at Trade Central. A layer saved before this update starts afresh at a CONTINUE. Where you said yes to the anonymous statistics, a run's end also counts its chips, good chips, Mystery Data opened and zenny earned. The numbers act by act are in docs/ECONOMY.md. (#154)

🛒 The Order Service sorts

AsterLand's clerk listed every chip of the Library by ID alone, five a page, while the folder editor and the Chip Trader beside him sort by seven keys. START on his list now goes on to the next of the same seven (ID, ABCDE, Code, Attack, Element, No., MB), each the way BN6 first sorts by it, and SELECT turns it around; his box names the sort over the buttons ("By Attack,high first!"). No. is how many of the chip, in its code, you hold. The list opens in your last sort again. Thanks to whitt-e for the request. (#124)

🔧 Fixed

  • A request pays once. An asker at home paid a settled request again after Lan jacked in at his PC and back out: the lab's man gave his 1000 zenny twice. BN6's jack-in rerolled its own maps' Mystery Data and cleared their flags, some of which are the run's (a request settled, the visit's order at AsterLand). Each layer now leaves BN6's own Mystery Data out of the roll. Thanks to Baine53 for the report. (#122)
  • Pads warp wherever MegaMan stands on them. BN6's own trigger behind a pad stops short of its art, so a player could stand on the pink pad in Lan's HP, or on the left of a layer's exit pad, and nothing happened. Every pad now warps from its art as drawn: the pink pad and the links in Lan's HP, a layer's exit pad, and the pad home in the Square. MegaMan still walks as BN6 walks him. (#161, #165)
  • The Recovery Mr.Prog keeps his patch for when you need it. At full HP he tells MegaMan to come back when he's hurt, where he used to spend the layer's one patch on him unasked; when MegaMan is hurt, he asks first. (#165)
  • A Trader on the map. Chip and BugFrag Traders have their own entry on a layer's map, apart from the shops. (#165)

Under the hood

A NetBattle is BN6's own Practice NetBattle on an emulated link cable: each game runs both players' GBAs from both players' keys, the MegaMan each run built written into his side, BN5's installs in both, and the two games compare a hash of the battle as it goes. The server only pairs the players and relays their keys; it is ROM-free and never runs a game. A rollback puts both GBAs back to a snapshot and runs the frames again with the keys that came. The New 3DS, which cannot keep up, was measured on the device before its pass was made to say so.

These notes with their pictures are on the project's website and GitHub.

1729051.html:
The tenth beta: the Net Square answers back. MegaMan performs every emote in his own BN6 poses and sounds, one press away on SELECT's strip or one tap on a second screen, and a wave gets its wave back. A NetBattle now runs from the ask to the result on PET screens, a rematch is back in the battle in about a second, and on a good link the input delay is down to one frame. And two players can team up: a relay one by one, or side by side, four MegaMen on one field.

👋 Say it with MegaMan

Emotes, performed

An emote is no longer a caption over a head: it is MegaMan's own BN6 pose and a sound of BN6's, the same on every screen. A hand raised for Wave, both arms up for Cheer, down on one knee for Bow, the item-get pose and jingle for Got it!, the buster held out, a collapse, a turn on the spot, sparks. A caption shows in BN6's chat box only where a pose can't say it ("Haha!", "Hmm..."). Twelve emotes, six of them new, and none of them ever moves MegaMan.

  • One press: hold L and press a direction for one of four favourites: up Wave, right Cheer, down Bow, left Laugh.
  • Wave and wave back: a Wave, Cheer or Bow sent while facing another MegaMan is aimed at him. A hand blinks over your name on his screen, and his next one answers you, whichever way he faces: within five seconds, BN6's "!!" and sparkle play between you two on everyone's screen. Past two unanswered at one player, the rest show on your screen alone, so nobody can be flooded with waves.
  • In step: every emote starts on the server's beat, so a group's emotes play together on every screen. The Square cheers back, and the more of you there are, the bigger: from three together the walking Navis cheer too, from four the greeter calls out as well.
  • A burst of three, then one a second (it was two, then one every two seconds). Quiet please in L's chat hides everyone else's.

(#176)

The emote strip, and a palette on the second screen

Emotes and phrases used to be pages of L's chat boxes away: 5 to 16 presses for an emote, 4 to 11 for a phrase. SELECT in the Net Square now opens the emote strip, a PET screen laid out as the Custom screen lays out its chips: the twelve emotes as MegaMan's own poses in two rows, the one under the cursor played by MegaMan in a window with its name and whom it goes to ("AT MIRA"), A to send, L and R to the eight phrases and back. An emote now takes 2 to 6 presses (4 on average), a phrase 3 to 6, and the last one again two, with no chat box typed out on the way.

  • Your own favourites: hold SELECT and press a direction on the strip to put the emote or phrase under the cursor on L and that direction. Phrases can be favourites too.
  • On a phone, SELECT's touch button opens the strip, and a tap sends.
  • On a second screen (the New 3DS's bottom screen, an Android handheld's lower one) every emote and phrase is a button, one tap each, with the NetPass on a tab beside them.

L's chat keeps Look around and Quiet please, and the first time it opens MegaMan points you to SELECT. (#178)

⚔️ NetBattles, from the ask to the result

Asking, and being asked

Before anyone commits, the Square now tells the truth about a challenge:

  • A challenge you sent shows at the top of your screen: his PET ringing, then his time to answer running down once he reads it, the link's bars beside it. Call off on his card takes it back, and Battle on anyone else meanwhile gets MegaMan's "we already asked".
  • The player you challenge hears his PET ring and sees a "!" over you. MegaMan reads him your MegaMan's card before "Take it,Lan?", and his 30 seconds start only once the question is up.
  • The link between two players shows as bars, never a number, beside a player's card and the question.
  • Busy marks: a small mark over a player says he is in a NetBattle (pulsing while the bout runs, as the referee calls it out), watching one, or at a trade.
  • A refused challenge (busy, gone, no stamp) is MegaMan's word in the chat box, no longer a notice in the corner.

(#167)

The way in and the result card

The way in is a PET Network panel instead of a black screen: both players, each MegaMan's HP, Crosses and Souls as carried, your set's score with this player, and whose PET is still on its way. On the Custom screen the other player's name sits on a small plate, and a link badge (bars only) shows the link steady, correcting a guess, or waiting. A wait past a second names whose PET it waits for, offers B to leave after ten seconds and ends by itself at twenty.

The battle ends on a result card instead of two lines on black: win or lose, the time, the HP each of you has left, the chips each used, the set's score, and the rematch asked right there, the other player's answer shown as it comes ("Kei wants another!"). A stop is the PET's word on the card, and a bout that broke off counts neither won nor lost: the referee calls it "BROKE OFF! NO CALL!". Short fades and BN6's own sounds take you in and out. (#167)

A rematch in about a second

Two Yeses on the result card go straight back into the battle. Each game keeps the two linked GBAs as the bout began and goes in from there: a few hundred frames instead of the whole way in. Each bout still deals its own hands and rolls, the same on both games and for every spectator, and the set's score keeps counting on the panel and the card. (#167)

Snappier NetBattles

Where both games can rewind as far as the trip takes, a NetBattle's input delay is now 1 frame instead of 2: every press, step and chip of your own lands a frame sooner. The other player's sounds stay whole when a guess of his keys is corrected, instead of going silent. And the games share their waits evenly, so the player on the worse link no longer sees the deeper corrections, and they are held where nobody sees them: on the Custom screen, or while your keys rest. (#167)

🤝 Team NetBattles

Team up

Where both players hold the Arena stamp, Team up on a player's card asks him to team up, his MegaMan asks Lan, and Split up on your partner's card ends it. The one who asked is the team's captain. Battle on a player of another team challenges his team, and MegaMan asks how to fight: One by one or Side by side. The other team hears which before it answers. (#167)

One by one: the relay

Each captain picks who goes first without seeing the other team's pick, then both orders are shown. The leads fight a NetBattle as ever; the winner stays on with the HP he has left, the loser's partner comes in, and a team is out when both its MegaMen are deleted. Whoever waits, and whoever is out, is taken to the stands to watch the bout, unasked. Between bouts the result card shows the MegaMen standing and who is next; at the end, the team's result. A leave or a dropped link mid-match breaks it off for both teams, with no result: nothing is won or lost. The referee calls a team's bouts.

Side by side: two MegaMen a side

Side by side, all four MegaMen fight on one field, two a side. Each team's captain leads and his partner stands beside him, and every one of the four games runs the same battle in BN6's own engine from the four players' buttons, rolling back as a NetBattle of two does.

  • His own Custom screen: each partner picks his chips on BN6's own Custom screen of his own game, from his own folder dealt into his own deck. The leads' screen waits for him by BN6's own link wait (the other side sees "Cstmzing..." over the side that waits), and a quiet sign tells a lead his partner is still picking, and a partner that his lead is ready. Once anyone has pressed OK, whoever is still picking has 30 seconds, then his picks so far are taken; only he sees a quiet sign in his last ten.
  • His whole MegaMan: a partner brings his NaviCust's programs (his HP, buster, abilities and the chips his screen deals), his Cross from his own CROSSSELECT, his Beast Out from his own emblem, a Program Advance made on his own screen, and UNITE with his own Souls. Under full rules BN5's Souls, mood and DarkChips answer for each MegaMan: a partner's charged B is his own while his lead is in a Chaos Unison, and a partner's mood, dark and DarkChip after-effects are his own.
  • Four players of different runs build the same battle, and a partner's choice his own Custom screen could not have made (a chip outside his hand, a Cross he lacks, a Soul he does not hold) is refused on every game alike.

The way in shows all four MegaMen, a partner's seat has its own HP box, and the result card shows each one's HP left and the team's WIN or LOSE. A stall says whose PET it waits for, and anyone else in the channel can watch from the stands. (#181)

🔧 Fixed

  • DarkInvs on the challenged player's side of a NetBattle. Under full rules, the second player's DarkInvs (or ShadowSoul's Chaos Unison, which uses it) moved his MegaMan's AI data into the block the first player's MegaMan already held: both MegaMen read one AI data, the first turned grey under the other's DarkInvs and the battle stood still. Each MegaMan now has a room of his own, so either player's DarkInvs takes his own MegaMan alone, both at once too, and a NetBattle without it is the battle it was. (#182)

Under the hood

Side by side, a partner's buttons and choices travel inside his lead's GBA's own link packets, BN6's own, so both linked GBAs read them in the same frame as the lead's: a partner who never picks, or all four in Beast Out, can no longer make the two GBAs see different battles. Each partner's NaviCust is worked out by BN6's own code over the battle's own starting state, never a player's save. A rematch's bout seed is its battle's ID, which both players and every spectator already know, so no new message carries it.

The network thread no longer rests between looks: it wakes when a key is put to go out or one comes in, and uses less CPU. Every client socket asks for no Nagle where the system lets it.

A 0.14.0 game speaks protocol v15 (0.13.0 spoke v10): a server and its games update together, and the gate says which side is behind. For hosts: the Arena's delay still comes from delay_for, now 1 at least, and the server pairs teams, their relays and the four seats of a side-by-side battle as it pairs two players, keeping them in memory only (server/README.md).

These notes with their pictures are on the project's website and GitHub.

1729053.html:
A point release for 0.14: a Jukebox in the PET with every song of BN6 and BN5, the title's music on BN6's own sound engine, Options a press away with a Display section, and the screens the game adds drawn as BN6 draws its PET.

🎵 The Jukebox

A new key item: KeyItem in the PET, then A on Jukebox. It plays every song of the game, BN6's 37, and with BN5's ROM beside it BN5's 35, as the cartridges play them: on BN6's own sound engine, which BN5 shares byte for byte. The game holds still while it is open and its music picks up where it was when you close it.

  • Sections by game and by where a song plays: Towns, The Net, Battles, Story and Screens. L and R (or Left and Right) turn them, A plays, B closes, and on a phone a tap on a song plays it.
  • Three modes on START: Repeat plays the song over and over, In order plays the section from the song on, and Shuffle plays the section in any order. A song that loops goes round twice before the next.
  • Its lights are the song's eight tracks as they sound. The last song and mode are kept for next time.

The names are ours, for where each song plays, checked against where the ROM plays it. Twelve of BN5's songs whose place we haven't found yet are in More by their number. If you know where they play, tell us.

🔊 The sound as the cartridge plays it

  • The title's music, note for note. The title, the run's setup, Options, SAVES and the PET's screens played BN6's songs on an approximation of the engine's own, duller than the game. They now play on BN6's own sound engine's rules, read from its code: its sequencer, its four channels and their priorities, its envelopes, the songs' reverb and its 8-bit mix, then the GBA's PSG and output as mGBA plays them. Laid beside the game frame by frame, it is the same, byte for byte, for every song and sound checked.
  • The music holds its pitch. The game's sound is nudged a hair faster or slower to stay in step with the speakers, and that nudge moved the pitch 10 to 18 cents from one frame to the next: a slight warble on every held note. It follows the average now, under a cent a frame.
  • The Legacy Collection's balance, if you like it. A player told us the sound felt off next to the Legacy Collection's. That collection plays CD recordings rather than the game's own sound, mixed softer. Options' Audio now has Sound: Soft, fitted to a recording of the Legacy Collection on the same songs: highs from 5 kHz up taken down (-10 dB at 10 kHz) and the deepest bass a little. GBA, the default, stays as the cartridge plays it. It changes at once so you can hear it, and the browser player's menu has a Sound button too.

⚙️ Options, a press away

  • OPTIONS on the title's menu, under NEW GAME and CONTINUE, in the title's own letters, and Options in the PET's menu during a run, in the place of BN6's Comm, which a run always greyed out. The game waits under it, and B brings you back to the PET where you were. SELECT on the title still opens it, and so does OPTIONS in a phone's touch menu.
  • A Display section: Fullscreen on a PC (borderless, as F11 and Alt+Enter, which now keep your choice too), Scale and Smooth motion. Scale is Auto (as before), Integer (whole pixels everywhere), Fill (as big as the screen holds, its shape kept: on a 1920x1080 screen no border above and below) or Stretch (the whole screen, the picture pulled to its shape). The 3DS has Fill, Integer and Stretch for its top screen. Thanks to Mooshymush for asking about the borders.

🖼️ The game's own screens look like BN6's PET

The screens the game adds to BN6 had a look of their own: a flat green band, thin teal panels on a dotted ground, bold letters everywhere. They are drawn to the measure of BN6's own PET screens now: the dark band with the screen's name and its stripes, the metal rails, windows framed in light and dark cyan round a navy field, the orange arrow for the cursor, key hints as E-Mail's START:SORT, notes in an information box like KeyItem's, and lists in BN6's own thin letters, read from your ROM. That covers the Jukebox, the NetPass, Trade Central, the NetBattle's cards, the wait for a dropped link, Options and the controls screen, the second screen, the ROMs screen and SAVES.

These notes with their pictures are on the project's website and GitHub.

1729054.html:
The eleventh beta: parts of the endless net go dark. From the second act, one way at the fork can lead to a layer gone dark, and taking it turns that layer into one of BN5's Liberation Missions, made afresh from the layer itself: a board of dark panels, DarkHoles and their guardians, and a Darkloid at the far end, liberated phase by phase against a par, in BN5's own look and sound. Beside it: the music off to play your own, a guardian's draft that knows what you hold, compression codes that stay entered, BN5's songs named, the Net Square as a hub, and the game's own screens closer still to BN6's.

🌑 Liberation Missions

One way has gone dark

From the second act, two forks in three at home hold a dark way: behind one of their two pads or links, a layer of the next act has gone dark. Its portal swirls in BN5's dark panels' shades, MegaMan says so when he reads the way ("And Lan... Part of it's gone dark. Dark panels,like Nebula's!"), and the act's card says "A layer here has gone dark". It is a risk you choose: the dark layer gives up the act's second Net Dealer and its Mr.Prog. The short net meets dark layers in acts 2 and 3, the endless net in acts 2 to 4.

The layer becomes a board

The dark layer is a Liberation Mission of BN5 Team Colonel's, made afresh from the layer's own floor, so no two boards are the same: dark panels, DarkHoles in their rings with a guardian on each (BigBrute, TinHawk, Bladia), item panels and BonusPanels, and a Darkloid, a Navi of BN6's, on his ring at the far end. As you arrive the camera goes to him and back, and Lan and MegaMan name the board: its DarkHoles and its par, the phases a planner took to clear it.

A battle for every panel

Each PLAYER PHASE MegaMan walks the clean panels as BN6 walks him and faces a dark one. A opens BN5's command window:

  • Liberation is a battle with BN5's three turns: TURN 1 START!, TURN 2 START!, FINAL TURN!. A win frees the panel, and a win in the first turn (1 TURN LIBERATE!) frees the dark around it too. When the final turn's gauge fills, TIME UP! and LIBERATE FAILED!: the panel stays dark.
  • LongSwrd spends an Order Point to free two panels in a line.
  • Pass rests.

Item panels give Order Points, hearts, chips or zenny; a BonusPanel spins BN5's roulette. A guardian fights in its own battle, and a DarkHole sends its deleted guardian back until the hole itself is liberated.

Then the dark strikes back

DARKLOID PHASE plays as BN5 plays it: the Darkloid first, his reach lit red, his line, his blow; then each guardian warps toward MegaMan and strikes, the camera going to each as it acts, and the harm in BN5's yellow digits. The board's harm never takes MegaMan's last HP.

Beat the par

Close every DarkHole and the Darkloid's ring can be liberated, and the Darkloid fought from it. Delete him and the exit opens where he stood, and the board pays for how fast you were: the fewer the phases against its par, the better the chip it leaves for the rest of the run. Each act adds one of BN5's rules: in act 3 a barrier and its key, with a sealed route behind it; in act 4 a roaming TinHawk and a barrier across the way. A planner plays every board as it is made, sets its par from its plays, and turns away boards with too many dead phases or nothing to decide.

In BN5's own look and sound

Everything on the board is BN5's, read from its ROM while the game runs (none of it is in the download): the board and its backdrop, the PLAYER PHASE and DARKLOID PHASE banners, the command window, the L view and its camera, the units animated, and BN5's board music; a battle won in its first turn ends on BN5's one-turn jingle. A CONTINUE goes on with the same board, phase and freed panels.

Liberation Missions need BN5 Team Colonel's ROM beside BN6's. MegaMan liberates alone for now; his teammates, the Navis whose Souls a run has won, come later. How the missions were taken apart and how the generator makes them: docs/LIBERATION.md.

🎛️ Smaller things, asked for by players

The music off, to play your own

Options' Audio has Music and Effects, each On or Off. Music off keeps BN6's sound effects while your own music plays; both off silences the game. It applies at once and is kept.

A guardian's draft knows what MegaMan holds

A player took UnderSht from Guardian Data while already holding it, more than once: BN6 sets UnderSht once, so a second does nothing. The draft now offers no program a copy would add nothing to (UnderSht, SuperArmor, the Shields, the shoes, the MAXes and the rest whose effect BN6 sets), and another of the build takes its place. A program that adds, like Custom1 or HP+50, shows how many you hold: "HP+50 (white) Held 1".

A compression code stays entered

A compression code was kept once entered, but its ten buttons had to be pressed again in every run, and a player said they ended up not using them. Now every program whose code you have entered in any run comes compressed as a run begins. Compressing never costs a fit, and the code entered again undoes it for that run, as in BN6. Dad's Compression mail still lists each code, and a code you have never entered is never applied.

BN5's songs, named

The Jukebox's BN5 songs had numbers in place of names, or names borrowed from BN6. Every song Team Colonel starts is now named for its own place, read from BN5's scripts: SciLab, Beach Day, A Stranger, Hope, Challenge, Area Liberated and One-Turn Win among them. In runs, BN5's own Before the Boss plays as a guardian logs in on BN5's areas, and a dark layer won plays BN5's song for a won mission.

🌐 The Net Square, a hub and its parts

Friends who visited together lost each other: the Square was one wide plaza with its wings out of sight. Now everyone arrives in a compact welcome plaza, its landmark in the middle, the pad home, the greeter, the keeper and the Board by the arrival. Three warps off its sides, BN6's own gem pads, go to Trade Central, the Arena (the ring and its stands) and the stage, each a small place of its own, the warp back right where MegaMan lands. Over each warp its name in gold and who is there now ("ARENA: Mira"); L's Look around says which way each warp lies and who is where. A part is a few seconds from the arrival and back.

A server and its players need 0.15.0 alike: a 0.14 game meeting the new Square is told a newer version is out.

🖥️ Closer to BN6's own screens

The JACK-IN SETUP

The setup after NEW GAME now sits in the PET window as Options does: BN6's orange arrows on each value, the row under the cursor explained in KeyItem's INFORMATION box, JACK IN! as the NaviCust's green RUN! at the foot of the list, and NEW in E-Mail's mark. The helpers have a page of their own: A on Help opens it, B goes back.

A run ends on BN6's RESULT

The summary after a run is two PET screens now, as BN6's battle RESULT gives its record and then what it got: RESULT (how the run ended and by whom, the layer reached, viruses and Navis deleted, and MegaMan's word in the NAVIGATOR box), then A to RECORDS (the Library and what the run added, the best, what the run opened marked NEW, and the closest goal), and A again for the title.

The PET's screens say as little as BN6's

BN6's own screens never show what A and B do, turn pages under small green arrows, and ask Yes or No behind a green triangle. The game's own screens now do the same: the key lines under the Jukebox, Options, the statistics question, Trade Central and the emote strip are gone, and Options' Display and Audio take the band's name as the folder editor takes CHIP FOLDER's. Only lists sit in the cyan window, as in BN6; a chip shows on the Library's grey card, buttons are STATUS's pills, and explanations sit in SubChip's flat panel. Each screen fades up from black as it opens, START on Trade Central's list opens a SORT pop-up as the folder editor's does, and in a chip trade MegaMan asks in BN6's NAVIGATOR box. The rules, measured from BN6's screens: docs/UI.md.

1729057.html:
A point release for 0.15: the Navis whose Souls a run holds now liberate beside MegaMan, the dark boards play as BN5's Liberation Missions piece by piece, a dark layer's secret opens a third way at the fork, and a fast forward button speeds up everything between fights and never the fights themselves.

⏩ Fast forward, outside the fight

A press of its button runs the game faster: walking a layer and the town, chats, fades and warps, a battle's opening and its results. Held, it runs only while held. From a battle's first Custom screen to its last deletion it is BN6's speed, always, and so are BN6's menus and online play: nothing you decide against the clock changes, and there the button does nothing and the touch controls' ▶▶ steps aside. Two of the PET's orange arrows show in the corner while it runs.

  • Its button: Tab or Space, a controller's right trigger or right stick press, ▶▶ on the touch controls. The controls screen has a FAST row for it. A controller's right trigger was R as well before; a pad.ini from before keeps it so.
  • Its speed: Options' new Fast forward line sets 2x, 3x (the default), 4x or off. The music keeps its pitch, and a machine that cannot go that fast goes as fast as it can.
  • The run's minutes count the game's own time now, so the week's DeepNet ranks a dive alike with fast forward or without.

Thanks to the player who asked for turbo because the game felt slow: the slow part was the time between decisions, not the battles.

🌑 Liberation Missions with a team

On a dark layer, the Navis whose BN5 Souls the run holds now join MegaMan on the board, as many as BN5's team of that stage holds: two at act 2, three at act 3, four at act 4. Each stands in his own BN5 body with BN5's HP for him.

  • A turn each, as BN5's team takes them. Play passes on after each Navi acts, R hands it to the next yet to act, and those who have acted stand darker.
  • Each brings his own command for an Order Point: Colonel's ScrenDiv frees three across, TomahawkMan's TomahawkSwing two deep and three wide, NumberMan's NumberCheck takes the items of the dark ahead with no battle, ShadowMan's SneakAttack weakens a guardian, ToadMan's LifeMelody lets a teammate beside him free five in a line, and KnightMan's StoneBody keeps harm off him and whoever stands beside him.
  • A teammate's battle is MegaMan in that Navi's Soul from the first turn, on that Navi's HP. Deleted there, he leaves the board and the run goes on.
  • The guardians and the Darkloid go for the nearest Navi. The boards are made for their team, as thick with dark as BN5's own of that stage, and a Pass now gives back a fifth of a Navi's HP, as BN5's does. A CONTINUE goes on with the same team where it stood.

🛣️ A third way, by the route found in the dark

The sealed route behind a Liberation board's locked barrier (acts 3 and 4) now leads somewhere. Free its key and the route, and at the next fork in Lan's HP a third portal lights at the link on the right: another area of the act's tier and a guardian the act's other ways do not have. Found on act 4's board in the endless net, or act 3's in the short net, it opens a second way into the Nest instead, to a different last boss: in the endless net, a Navi in the Cybeast's place, with its HP. A route not taken at its fork is spent; a CONTINUE keeps it.

🗺️ Liberation Missions as BN5 plays them

Each piece traced in BN5's own ROM and laid beside it.

Each board in its own mission's look

A dark layer is drawn in the BN5 mission its area takes, its map, backdrop and colours, where every board had mission 1's.

The board's HP

Every unit's HP stands under it in BN5's white digits. The Darkloid keeps his HP between battles: a battle that leaves him standing leaves him hurt, and he heals at the start of his turn by the dark round him, BN5's rising lines over him.

The guardians strike and return as BN5's

TinHawk's HawkAttack warps beside its Navi and back, Bladia's DarkSlash and the Darkloid's blow burst over him, and a deleted guardian rises on its DarkHole and warps beside it, as BN5 brings him back.

The battle on BN5's field

The dark round a panel sets the field, up to Surrounded: foes on both sides, and L or R turns MegaMan round. The Custom screen opens by itself as the gauge fills, and the Darkloid's battle has BN5's three turns too.

BonusPanels

Liberation frees one without a battle or the Navi's turn, then BN5's roulette spins its five slots until A stops it: no harm this phase, HP full, five Order Points, a chip, or Major Hit.

A board won, as BN5 ends one

  • The words: the Darkloid speaks as his first turn begins, L's map view has BN5's keys and shows the guardians' reach, and a board won ends with BN5's SUCCESS! and MegaMan's tally of the target and the phases taken.
  • The prize in BN5's tiers: two phases under par or better a chip, at par a lesser one, over par zenny.

BN5's own Darkloids

BlizzardMan and ShadeMan hold boards of BN5's areas, in their own sprites, faces and battles, matched to BN5's frame by frame.

🎮 On itch.io

Cyberworld Endless has a page on itch.io: https://saschb2b.itch.io/cyberworld-endless, with the browser game and every system's download.
